Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:11:1.english: He rolls it - once every twelve months.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:11:2.english: If he opened it for himself - [The Gemara] explains all of it further on.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:12:1.english: Why specifically a scroll - For it is easily ruined through smudging and tearing.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:12:2.hebrew: כאן שנה רבי - במסכת גיטין (דף כט.) תנן: השולח גט בארץ ישראל הרי זה משלחו ביד אחר, ואם אמר לו טול חפץ פלוני הימנה — לא ישלחנו ביד אחר, שאין רצונו שיהא פקדונו ביד אחר. ואמר ר"ל עלה: כאן שנה רבי — במשנה זו למדנו רבי שסתם המשניות: אין השואל כו', דבכולהו שייך למימר אין רצונו שיהא פקדונו ביד אחר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:12:2.english: Here Rabbi taught - In Tractate Gittin (29a), we learned [in a Mishnah]: "One who sends a bill of divorce in the Land of Israel may send it through another [agent]; but if [the husband] said to him, 'Take such-and-such an object from her,' he may not send it through another [agent], because he does not want his deposit to be in the hands of another [person]." And Reish Lakish said regarding it: "Here Rabbi taught" — in this Mishnah, Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who redacted the anonymous Mishnahs, taught us: "A borrower is not [allowed to lend]," etc., for in all of [these cases] it is applicable to say, "He does not want his deposit to be in the hands of another [person]."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:15:1.hebrew: מאי עבידתיה גביה - קס"ד לצורכו קאמר ולא לצורך ספר תורה, דהא לצורך ספר תורה תנא ליה: גוללו כל שנים עשר חדש. להכי פרכינן: מאי עבידתיה דהאי גבי ספר תורה לקרות בו לצורך עצמו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:15:1.english: What is his business with it - [The Gemara] initially assumed [that the baraita] means for his own need and not for the need of the Torah scroll, for [regarding] the need of the Torah scroll it [already] taught: "He rolls it every twelve months." Therefore, we ask: What business does this [bailee] have with the Torah scroll, to read from it for his own need?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:15:2.hebrew: אם כשהוא גוללו - להנאת ס"ת פתחו וקרא בו, מותר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:15:2.english: If, when he is rolling it - [meaning,] for the benefit of the Torah scroll he opened it and read from it, it is permitted.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:16:1.english: In [the case of] a new [scroll], thirty days - The new [scroll] becomes moldy more quickly than the old [one].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:16:2.hebrew: אימא אחד זה ואחד זה שלשים יום - ומתני' נמי, דקתני קורא בהן אחת לשלשים יום ולא מפליג בין ישן לחדש, ר"א בן יעקב היא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:16:2.english: Say: Both this and that [are] thirty days - And our Mishnah as well, which teaches [that] one reads from them once every thirty days and does not distinguish between an old [scroll] and a new [one], is [the opinion of] Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:18:1.hebrew: בענין אחד - בפרשה אחת, אין קורין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:18:1.english: In one matter - In one section, yes, they [may] read [together].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:18:2.hebrew: בשני ענינים - זה בדף זה וזה בדף זה, קורין, דלא אתי לשמוטי מהדדי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:18:2.english: In two matters - [Where] this one is on this column and that one is on that column, they may read [together], for they will not come to pull [the scroll] from one another.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:19:1.english: One who has a skilled weaver in his house - Who will weave new garments for him continually.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:19:2.english: [He] may shake his garment every day - And we learn proper conduct, that shaking is harmful to it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:1:1.english: In accordance with Rabbah - In the chapter [entitled] HaZahav (below, Bava Metzia 58a), regarding the townspeople who sent their shekels.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:20:1.hebrew: בחד - באדם אחד, אין ניעורו קורעה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:20:1.english: With one - By one person, its shaking does not tear it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:20:2.hebrew: שנים - האוחזין בשני ראשיה ומנערין, ממתחין אותה יותר מדאי וקשה לה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:20:2.english: Two [people] - who hold [the garment] by its two ends and shake [it] stretch it excessively, and it is harmful to it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:22:1.english: Of wool - [shaking] is harmful to it, for it stretches and tears.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:23:1.hebrew: כסא דחרשין - נוח לשתות כוס של מכשפות מכוס של מים פושרין, ואיידי דאיירי במילי דרבי יוחנן בהלכות דרך ארץ, נקט הני שמעתא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:23:1.english: A cup of witches - It is better to drink a cup of witches than a cup of lukewarm water. And since [the Gemara] was discussing statements of Rabbi Yochanan regarding rules of proper conduct, it cites these teachings.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:23:3.hebrew: ציביא - כל דבר שנותנין לתוך המשקה, או עשבים או תבלין או עקרי בשמים, קרי ציביא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:23:3.english: Tzivya - Anything that one puts into the beverage — whether herbs, spices, or roots of aromatics — is called tzivya.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:24:1.hebrew: ורוצה לאבדן - ללמדנו בא שלא ירגיל אדם בכך, שהעושה אלה מאבד מהר הון רב:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:24:1.english: And he wishes to lose them - [He] comes to teach us that a person should not accustom himself to this, for one who does these [things] quickly loses great wealth.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:24:2.english: Roman linen - Their price is high and they wear out quickly.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:24:3.english: Explain it - [This refers] to this hiring of laborers.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:3:1.english: In [the case of] money of a lost item - That he sold it after he tended to it, as the Sages said.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:3:2.english: But lost coins - For example, if he found coins in a purse, or three coins arranged like towers.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:4:1.hebrew: אחת לשלשים יום - שמתעפשין כששוהים מלפותחן, וכל ספרים שלהן היו עשויין בגליון:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:4:1.english: Once in thirty days - For they become moldy when one delays opening them, and all their books were made in scroll [form].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:4:2.english: He rolls them - From their beginning to their end, so that air will enter them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:4:3.hebrew: בתחלה - מה שלא למד, מפני שצריך להשהותו לפניו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:4:3.english: For the first time - That which he has not [previously] studied, because he needs to leave it [open] before him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:4:4.hebrew: ולא יקרא אחר עמו - לפי שזה מושך אצלו, וזה מושך אצלו, ונקרע:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:4:4.english: And another shall not read with him - Because this one pulls [it] toward himself and that one pulls [it] toward himself, and it gets torn.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:5:1.english: He spreads it out for its sake - [To allow] air to take hold in it, so that it will not decay and moths will not eat it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:6:1.hebrew: לצרכן - שמתעפשים בקרקע, שצריך לתתן בקרקע כדאמרינן לקמן שזו היא שמירתן, ולפיכך משתמש בהם לפרקים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:6:1.english: For their [own] sake - For they corrode in the ground, as one must place them in the ground — as we say later that this is their [proper] safekeeping — and therefore he uses them occasionally.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:6:2.hebrew: אבל לא לשחקן - לא ישתמש בהן זמן ארוך שישחקן, אוזי"ר בלע"ז:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:6:2.english: But not to wear them out - He should not use them for a long time such that he wears them out; user in Old French.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:6:3.hebrew: לא יגע בהן - זהב אינו מתעפש בארץ, וזכוכית שמא ישבר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:6:3.english: He may not touch them - Gold does not corrode in the ground, and glass [may not be used] lest it break.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:7:1.hebrew: שאין דרכו ליטול - דבר שגנאי הוא לו, שאדם חשוב הוא ואין דרכו ליטול קופה שלו להכניסה מן החוץ לבית שמור, לא יטול, ופטור מהשבת אבידה, דילפינן מוהתעלמת:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:7:1.english: That it is not his manner to take - Something that is unbecoming for him — for he is a distinguished person and it is not his manner to take his [own] basket to bring it in from the outside into a guarded house — he shall not take [it], and he is exempt from returning a lost item, as we derive from "and you hide yourself."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:9:1.hebrew: בי בר חבו - בבית פלוני העושה תפילין, מצויין לימכר, ויחזור ויקנה מן הדמים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 29b:9:1.english: At the house of bar Ḥavu - In the house of so-and-so who makes tefillin, [they are] readily available for sale, and he can go back and buy [new ones] with the money.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 29b:6:1.hebrew: בזכוכית לבנה - וא"ת, והא אמרינן פרק עגלה ערופה (סוטה דף מח.) דמשחרב בית המקדש בטלה זכוכית לבנה? וי"ל דלא בטלה לגמרי קאמר, אלא דלא שכיחא; דהא רב הונא תבר זכוכית חיורתא בחופת בנו, פ' אין עומדין (ברכות דף לא. ע"ש):
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 29b:6:1.english: White glass - And if you will say: Behold, we say [in] the chapter Eglah Arufah (Sotah 48a) that from the time the Temple was destroyed, white glass ceased [to exist]? One can answer that it does not mean it ceased completely, rather that it is uncommon; for behold, Rav Huna broke white glass at his son's wedding canopy, [in] the chapter Ein Omdin (Berakhot 31a, see there).
